title: Prairie Engine Works
tagline: Build an engine part by part, put it on the dyno, then go racing.
summary: Longlight's biggest game so far. Put an engine together on the test stand, fire it up and hear it run, then take it to the drag strip or a truck and tractor pull to earn cash and reputation.
latest: A drag-strip announcer who calls your runs, and team seasons in the career

shots.alt: The build screen: a custom inline-4 with its power, torque, weight and cost
A finished dyno pull: 109 hp, with the power and torque curves
A finished engine certified as Marginal, with its stress report
The analysis screen listing how the parts you picked interact

start: Tap Career on the first screen; on your first visit a short First Fire run has you tap Start, then Run, to break and fix an engine.
When the tour opens on the Team tab, tap Sign with… on an offer, then on Build pick a green-tagged Starter engine within its class rules and budget.
Tap Run for a dyno pull to certify it, then on the Team tab tap Close week or To race week until Race round 1 appears.
tips: If the dyno breaks something, open the Analysis tab: the teardown names one change that fixes the failed part, and Use it fits it for you.
For more help, tap the Settings button, then Lessons, for 17 short guided tours that run on a scratch engine and put your own build back.
Autosave only keeps your game on this device, so open Settings, then Save, and tap Back up to get a code you can Restore on any phone.
guide.mistake: If you tap Close week on race week with no engine built for the team, the team sits the round out. The game asks first, so cancel and certify an engine with a clean dyno pull.

title: Scrapline
tagline: Build a combat robot under the weight limit and fight it in the arena.
summary: A combat robot builder. Design a fighting robot under a weight limit, test it on the bench, drive it in the arena, patch it in the pit and read the post-mortem, from a plywood box in a rented corner of a machine shop to the televised Scrapline Open.
latest: A balance pass on flippers, drums, lifters and the small-class pits

shots.alt: The build sheet: a beetleweight with a vertical spinner, 19 grams under the limit
The bench, where seven tests prove a robot before it fights
A fight in the arena, seen from above, with both robots' damage panels
Two robots trading hits beside the pit

start: Tap Career on the home screen, then Show me for a coached first fight of about five minutes on a loaner bot that leaves your workshop alone.
When it ends, tap Back to my workshop, then Start a career on the Career tab; you begin with €2,500, hand tools and a rented corner.
On Build, tap Fit to pay for your bot, enter this week's event from the Career tab, then tap Close week to bring in new workshop hours.
tips: Sparring on the Fight tab is free practice, even in a career: nothing is charged and nothing is kept, so try ideas there first.
After a fight, read the post-mortem and tap its Fix it button to jump straight to the Build row that needs changing.
To keep a backup, open Settings, find Saves and tap Back up to get a code you can paste into Restore on another phone.
guide.mistake: Changing parts only edits a draft, and the bot you fitted is the one that goes to an event, damage and all. Tap Fit, then Fit again on the bill, before you enter.

title: Season Ticket
tagline: Own a football club and change tactics while the match plays.
summary: A soccer club management game set in Valmere, a made-up northern country. Own a club in the 16-team Kestrel Football League: run the business from your own 3D office, build the squad and the stadium, and change tactics while you watch the match. Play a whole career, on your phone, even offline.
latest: A Settings screen on the title, and a loading screen

shots.alt: The manager's office with the laptop showing finances, the desk lamp and the trophy shelf
The lineup screen with a formation on the pitch and the tactics settings beside it
A live 3D match with modelled players defending the edge of the box and the match stats beside it
The Stadium tab with the 3D ground and the stand upgrade options
The same ground at night, with the town lit up round it

start: On the title screen tap Start a career, choose Easy, Normal, Hard or Very hard, then tap a club; easy clubs have money and a good squad.
On Make it yours, set the name, colours and crest, decide the homegrown rule now because it is fixed for the career, then tap Start the career.
Set your team on the Squad and Lineup tabs, then tap the big top-right button: Next week, or Match day to play, or Quick sim to skip watching.
tips: Renew players on the Squad tab before their contracts run out, or they leave for nothing at the end of the season.
Buy players on the Market tab while a transfer window is open (pre-season and the mid-season break); a Window open label shows in the top bar.
To keep a backup, tap your club's name at the top left to open the menu, tap Save code, then Copy or Save backup file.
guide.mistake: If your cash stays below zero, the lenders step in, and they are the only way to lose the club. Watch the cash figure in the top bar and get it back above zero quickly.

title: Funded
tagline: Pass a prop-firm challenge without breaking the daily loss limit.
summary: A prop-firm trading game. The firm gives you $25,000 and five days: hit the target without breaking the daily loss limit or the drawdown floor. Pass to climb to the $50k futures desk, then $100k options, picking edge cards for the career as you go.
latest: Three trading desks, edge cards and mandates

shots.alt: A trading day: the price chart with a news line, a long position up $186, and the BUY, SELL and FLATTEN buttons
Pick an edge: three cards to keep for the career, Stop Discipline, Hot Hand and Coffee
Day 1 closed, up $200, with the balance, days counted, distance to target and the drawdown floor

start: On the title screen, tap Start training day, then follow the coach bubbles, tapping Next or the button they point at, like BUY or FLATTEN.
When training ends, tap Start your eval: the firm gives you $25,000 and five days to make +$1,500 without breaking a rule.
On each day card, tap Open the market, pick a size (25%, 50% or MAX), then trade with BUY, SELL and FLATTEN through the 3-minute day.
tips: The ◆ marks on the chart's time axis show when news will land, but not which way the price will jump.
Keep an eye on the LOSS, DD and TGT meters, because losing $750 in a day or touching the drawdown floor gets you fired.
A day only counts if you make at least one trade, and you need 3 counted days before you can pass.
guide.mistake: Holding any position at the 16:00 closing bell gets you fired on the spot. When the BELL countdown appears in the last 20 seconds, tap FLATTEN.

title: Lombard
tagline: Run a canal-side pawn shop: inspect, spot the fakes, haggle.
summary: A first-person pawn shop sim on a canal in Mostograd, a made-up Russian river city in the 2010s. Inspect what people bring in, spot the fakes, haggle, and decide how much trouble a good deal is worth.
latest: A pawn-ticket loading screen and a home screen icon

shots.alt: A customer at the counter with a soprano ukulele and a story about learning songs online
Inspecting a silver 1924 coin, with the loupe, scale, magnet and reference book below
Setting a price estimate on the keypad while the customer waits
The Evening Mostograd front page announcing the shop's new owner

start: On the title screen, tap an empty slot under Careers, name your shop or keep Lombard No. 7, then tap Next.
Tap Next through the short story cards (or Skip), then Begin, then Open shop, and Open the door if the morning paper appears.
When a customer walks in, tap Inspect, check the item with the Loupe, Scale and Magnet, then type its worth, tap Set estimate and make your Offer.
tips: Every tool costs time on the shop clock, and people in the queue give up and leave if you take too long.
On day 1 the clock stops while you inspect an item and type a price, so use that day to learn the tools.
Before your first buy on day 1 the reference book's price range is shown free; after that, tap Reference to see a range.
guide.mistake: Paying too much for a fake is the main way to lose money, so check with the tools and start from the 40% or 60% keys, which work from your own estimate. Don't go much lower: an offer under about a quarter of what the seller thinks it's worth is an insult.

title: Burn Rate
tagline: Design a solid rocket motor to spec, fire it, learn why it missed.
summary: A rocket motor design game. Rent a stand on an old state test range, design a solid motor to a client's spec, predict its curve, then fire it and find out why the real one didn't match.
latest: A Job button on the bench

shots.alt: The work-order board: a rocketry club wants a G motor for field day, with the impulse and burn time it needs and the pay
The design bench: the predicted pressure and thrust curves for an M motor, its numbers, and the propellant grades to choose from
An M motor firing on Stand 1 at dusk, with live pressure and thrust drawn over the predicted curves
The range report: a B pass, the measured curves with a casting void marked, and why it differed from the bench

start: On the title screen, tap New career, name your startup, then tap Sign the lease to start on Stand 3 with 2 500 cr.
On Work orders, tap Take the job on A G for field day, then To the bench, and tap Got it on each coach card.
Clear the red flag with a bigger Throat diameter on the Nozzle tab, tap To the stand, pick a slot, then Clear the range and fire.
tips: Designing on the bench is free; only a firing costs a range day, the stand's fee and the motor's materials, so tune until the flags clear.
Dawn fires cold grain and Noon fires hot grain, which changes the burn, so tap the temperature chip on the bench to predict at your slot.
If you're stuck, tap Job on the bench, then Hint: it costs 5% of the pay (at least 50 cr) and is free after 2 misses on that job.
guide.mistake: Firing a motor with a red flag still costs a range day, the fee and materials, and on the first job it bursts. Fix it with a bigger throat, because a thicker wall alone makes it burn out too fast for the spec.

title: Bump Stop
tagline: Build a rally truck, find the speed where it breaks, then go racing.
summary: A rally-raid truck builder. Build the truck part by part, run it on the test track until the suspension gives up, read why it broke, tune it, then send it into a multi-day raid where damage stacks from stage to stage. Light 4x4s, heavy trucks and side-by-sides across Birchland, a made-up northern country, summer and winter, in a career from 1985 to 2025.
latest: Damage you can see: mud, dust, snow and dents on the trucks

shots.alt: The build screen: a white light 4x4 with magenta springs, the three classes to pick from and the year slider at 1985
A run on the washboard ladder at 50 km/h, the truck close up in 3D with each corner's oil heat, travel and wear round the edges
The rear left shock goes over the limit: damper fade on lap 9 at 80 km/h, with the slow-motion replay
The report: damper fade on the rear left, what the crew chief says, and the oil temperature trace
Picking a raid and a driver: Blackfly Classic, Washboard 800, Cold Start 300 or Frozen Knuckle, with four drivers to choose from

start: On the Career tab, tap Start a career in 1985. A first-job guide walks you through the whole loop and ticks each step off as you go.
Take the privateer's job, then on the Build tab open Tires and fit studded ones that fit their budget: the first raid runs on ice and snow.
On the Test tab, pick Washboard ladder and tap Run until it breaks, read the report, tap a fix and run it again, then Hand it over.
tips: The washboard ladder goes 5 km/h faster every lap, so it finds the speed where your truck gives up. The report's fixes jump straight to the part or slider to change.
Damper heat is the big one: watch each corner's oil go from Normal to Warm to Over the limit. Fewer clicks of rebound makes less heat.
On a raid, Push is faster but cooks the shocks and wears the parts. Carry spares, and use the bivouac each night to patch the truck.
guide.mistake: Sending a truck out with no spares. Every roadside fix becomes a bodge that costs time, and the damage carries over to the next stage.

title: Frontier Lab
tagline: Found an AI lab and grow it across the world's tech capitals.
summary: An AI-lab tycoon. Raise a seed round, open sales offices, buy compute or build data centers, train your own models and ship products, keep the safety regulator happy, then take the lab public and grow it across the world's tech capitals, all on an engraved isometric city map.

title: Hull Down
tagline: Design a tank against a weight limit and send it to trial.
summary: A tank design game. Run a state design bureau, build a tank part by part against a weight limit, and send the prototype to trial. When it fails, the after-action report shows why.

title: Laminar
tagline: Prove a shape in the wind tunnel, then see if the tunnel was right.
summary: An aerodynamics consultancy game. Shape a design in 3D, build a scale model, prove it in the wind tunnel, then find out at the real event whether your tunnel told the truth. Riders, skaters, ski jumpers, bobsleds, trucks, race cars, record cars, drones and aircraft, from 2010 to 2040.

The Shape screen: a time-trial rider on a bike in 3D with teal handles to reshape, the desk estimate, comfort, frontal area and rules cards, and the position sliders

The wind tunnel in dark mode: the smoke rake and tufts showing the flow round the rider, above the fan and yaw dials

title: Crumple
tagline: Design the parts that fold, crash it, and keep the cabin whole.
summary: A crash-lab game. Design the parts of a car that fold in a crash, fire it down the sled, watch it crumple in slow motion, read what the dummy felt, tune the structure and crash it again. Then the carmaker builds it and the official test decides its star rating. A small crash-structure firm in a made-up country's car industry, 1970 to 2010. Dummies only.
